items.title: Being locally of finite presentation is fpqc local on the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property 'f is locally of finite presentation' is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 5983-5987). The proof records base-change stability and Zariski locality, then reduces to a flat surjective morphism of affines: for an affine open U of X the base change U' is affine of finite type over S', and writing S = Spec(R), S' = Spec(R'), U = Spec(A), U' = Spec(A') the situation becomes the faithfully flat ring map R -> R' with A' = R' tensor_R A and R' -> A' of finite presentation, so the descent lemma for finite presentation gives that R -> A is of finite presentation; the general locality lemma concludes (proof lines 5989-6010). The level is H2: the reduction to the affine ring-theoretic statement is short and complete, and the single descending input is a standard algebra lemma.
